comparison: Both address RNA-seq findings (C5, C44-C47, C95). OpenEval finds the data well-supported with adequate methodology. Peer reviewers express concern that the experiment was conducted at 12 months (advanced disease stage), questioning whether endo-lysosomal dysfunction is primary or secondary pathology, thus rating UNCERTAIN vs OpenEval's SUPPORTED.

Both address early endosome enlargement (C6, C50, C126). OpenEval finds the immunohistochemistry data well-supported with appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers describe findings as 'compelling' and accept the detailed characterization. Both agree this is SUPPORTED.

Both address BDNF and TrkB accumulation in early endosomes (C9, C51, C53-C55). OpenEval finds the data well-supported by immunohistochemistry. Peer reviewers acknowledge findings but raise significant concerns about 'specificity of BDNF and TrkB immunostaining,' noting detection difficulties despite added controls, rating UNCERTAIN vs OpenEval's SUPPORTED.

OpenEval addresses mechanistic inferences about BDNF/TrkB sequestration (C56-C57) rating UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct measurement. Peer R10 addresses broader conclusions about trafficking defects and signaling (C37-C38, C52, C56-C57, C120-C121) rating SUPPORTED, accepting the connection as a major contribution despite OpenEval's caution about specific mechanistic claims.

Both address TrkB trafficking defects (C63-C64). OpenEval finds strong support from dual-compartment analysis showing increased TrkB in early endosomes and decreased in recycling endosomes. Peer reviewers accept that 'TrkB recycling to the cell membrane in recycling endosomes is reduced' as part of detailed characterization. Both rate SUPPORTED.

Both address late endosome defects (C7, C70, C72-C73). OpenEval finds the Rab7 and BDNF data well-supported, though notes C73-C74 are somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'late endosome transport of BDNF for degradation was impaired' as part of the characterization. Both rate SUPPORTED.

Both address lysosome analysis (C76-C90). OpenEval finds comprehensive support from dual-labeling approach showing no significant differences in lysosome markers. Peer reviewers accept these findings as establishing compartment-specific pathology rather than global disruption. Both rate SUPPORTED.

OpenEval addresses late endosome precursors (C91-C92) rating SUPPORTED. Peer R7 addresses broader trafficking and lysosomal dysfunction (C8, C91-C94, C100-C102, C108-C109), explicitly accepting that 'Purkinje cells have impaired ability to degrade endocytosed cargo beyond BDNF and TrkB' due to trafficking deficits. Both rate SUPPORTED with overlapping claims.

OpenEval synthesizes trafficking impairment findings (C8, C93-C96) rating SUPPORTED, though notes lysosomal dysfunction inference is speculative given normal morphology. Peer R7 explicitly accepts the interpretation of 'trafficking deficits that result in disruption in transport to lysosomes and lysosomal dysfunction.' Agreement on trafficking defects, peer reviewers more accepting of lysosomal dysfunction claim.

OpenEval addresses Pepstatin A experiments (C98-C103) rating SUPPORTED for trafficking interpretation but notes activity claims are speculative. Peer R7 accepts these findings as part of broader evidence for impaired cargo degradation beyond BDNF/TrkB. Both rate SUPPORTED with overlapping interpretation.

OpenEval addresses CTSD upregulation and compensatory mechanisms (C104-C107) rating UNCERTAIN due to speculative interpretations. Peer R1 shares temporal concerns about whether findings represent primary or secondary events, though addresses different claim set. Both express uncertainty about mechanistic interpretations.

OpenEval addresses general trafficking deficit beyond BDNF/TrkB (C108-C109) rating SUPPORTED. Peer R7 explicitly accepts this interpretation, stating cells have 'impaired ability to degrade other endocytosed cargo beyond BDNF and TrkB.' Strong agreement on this conclusion.

Both address 7,8-DHF rescue effects (C12, C117-C119). OpenEval finds the rescue data well-supported though mechanism unclear. Peer reviewers acknowledge rescue effect but raise substantial concerns about 7,8-DHF mechanism, citing studies questioning its role as TrkB agonist and suggesting antioxidant/anti-inflammatory effects instead. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, peer rates UNCERTAIN due to mechanistic doubts.

Both address prior 7,8-DHF work and mechanistic claims (C110-C116). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as appropriately cited context with clearly identified speculation. Peer reviewers explicitly question the mechanism, stating beneficial effects 'may be caused by 7,8-DHF properties other than the putative agonist role on TrkB' and conclude 'it is most unlikely that mechanistically this occurs through a TrkB agonistic effect.' Major disagreement on mechanism.

OpenEval addresses summary synthesis (C120-C123) rating SUPPORTED with C122 noted as speculative. Peer R10 addresses overlapping conclusions (C120-C121 plus others) and accepts the connection between trafficking defects and signaling deficits as 'valuable insights' and a 'major contribution.' Both rate SUPPORTED for main conclusions.

Both address timing and causality (C139-C140). OpenEval finds the early timing argument well-supported though notes causality not directly demonstrated. Peer R11 accepts findings as 'compelling and significant' but this aligns with their temporal concerns in R1 about whether defects are primary or secondary. Both acknowledge importance while noting causality limitations.

OpenEval addresses prior model characterization (C37-C43) rating SUPPORTED as appropriately cited context. Peer R10 references some of these claims (C37-C38) as part of accepting the overall contribution. Both agree these provide essential background.
OpenEval addresses SCA6 background literature (C1-C4, C15-C18) rating SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background material.
OpenEval addresses endo-lysosomal system background (C19-C28) rating SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background material.
OpenEval addresses endo-lysosomal dysfunction in other diseases background (C29-C36) rating SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background material.
OpenEval addresses BDNF/TrkB trafficking background (C39, C58-C59, C66-C67, C75, C97) rating SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background material.

OpenEval addresses discussion points and novelty claims (C126-C138) rating SUPPORTED. Peer R11 addresses overlapping claims about novelty and significance (C133, C137-C140), stating findings are 'compelling and significant' and 'crucial in understanding underlying pathology.' Both rate SUPPORTED for the contribution's significance.
